plugins.plugin.name: Plugin center
plugins.page.title: Plugins
plugins.page.lead: Manage plugins; click a card for details and configuration
plugins.action.restartTip: Restart the host to reload the plugin directory
plugins.action.restartTipBrowser: Restarting the host is available in the desktop app only
plugins.group.packagesHint: packages installed in the profile (package.json pneuma.client.platform = pneuma); installing means consent, so this only toggles them
plugins.group.officialHint: Shipped with the app; turn on demand, click a card to configure
plugins.group.kernelHint: Part of Pneuma itself; cannot be disabled
plugins.empty.lead: Click “+ Add plugin” at the top right to pick a .js file, or drop it into
plugins.card.capabilities: UI capabilities (dsh client plugins): {list} · listed only, not loaded
plugins.card.locked: Part of the runtime kernel; cannot be disabled
plugins.problem.version.label: Version mismatch
plugins.problem.version.next: Upgrade the host (shell) to satisfy the @dsc/ui range the plugin declares, or ask the author to change plugin.json's api to a range this shell supports.
plugins.problem.artifact.label: Artifact unreadable
plugins.problem.artifact.next: Check that ~/.dsc/plugins/<dir>/ui/client.js exists and is readable (directory and file names must match case exactly); reinstall the plugin if it is missing.
plugins.problem.manifest.label: Manifest incomplete
plugins.problem.manifest.next: Check ~/.dsc/plugins/<dir>/plugin.json: the file must exist and declare api (an @dsc/ui range such as "^1.0.0").
plugins.problem.clash.label: Name clashes with a built-in
plugins.problem.clash.next: Rename the plugin directory so it differs from any built-in plugin id.
plugins.problem.stale.label: Content changed; confirm again
plugins.problem.stale.next: This plugin's files changed after you approved them (an upgrade, a reinstall, or an edit). Once you confirm it is the build you want, confirm once on this card and it loads.
plugins.problem.packageVersion.label: Version mismatch
plugins.problem.packageVersion.next: Upgrade the host (shell) to satisfy the @dsc/ui range this package declares, or release the package for a shell version you run.
plugins.problem.packageArtifact.label: Entry unreadable
plugins.problem.packageArtifact.next: Check this package's package.json: exports["./client"] must point to a file that really exists inside the package (reinstall the package if it is broken).
plugins.problem.packageManifest.label: Manifest incomplete
plugins.problem.packageManifest.next: Check this package's package.json: pneuma.client.platform must be "pneuma" and pneuma.client.api must be set (e.g. "^2.0.0").
plugins.problem.packageClash.label: Name clashes with an existing plugin
plugins.problem.packageClash.next: This package name matches a built-in plugin (or another UI plugin) id, so it cannot join the boot graph; rename it or disable the clashing one first.
plugins.problem.packageStale.label: Content changed; confirm again
plugins.problem.packageStale.next: This package's UI artifact changed after it was loaded. Once you confirm it is the build you want, reinstall it or confirm again in the plugin centre.
plugins.problem.unknownTrust.label: Install failed
plugins.problem.unknownTrust.next: Following the reason above, check plugin.json and ui/client.js under ~/.dsc/plugins/<dir>/.
plugins.problem.unknownPackage.label: Install failed
plugins.problem.unknownPackage.next: Following the reason above, check this package's package.json (the `pneuma.client` section) and exports["./client"].
plugins.trust.packageDesc: The bundle ships its own UI half; installing it in a profile counts as consent—this only toggles it, and both directions take effect immediately
plugins.trust.trustedDesc: Trusted; you can toggle it (both directions take effect immediately)
plugins.trust.untrustedDesc: Untrusted: no trust record yet—confirm once in the plugin center on first install (it will be able to call the host's UI methods)
plugins.trust.disclosureTitle: What it can do once trusted
plugins.trust.currentHost: (current shell v{version}; the gate blocks it and explains why when unmet)
plugins.trust.capabilities: Capabilities: whitelisted host UI-channel methods; in the desktop window the native bridge is available (open directories, terminal, and so on)
plugins.trust.effect: Effect: loads after confirmation, and enable/disable takes effect immediately (the shell and renderer are the only exceptions: refresh the page)
plugins.err.readTrust: Failed to read third-party UI plugin status: {message}
plugins.err.trustDesktopOnly: Confirming trust writes ~/.dsc/plugins.json, which only the desktop app can do (a browser has no such bridge)
plugins.err.restartDesktopOnly: Restarting the host uses the desktop shell's native bridge, which a browser does not have
plugins.err.installDesktopOnly: Installing a plugin uses the desktop shell's file picker, which a browser does not have
plugins.detail.noConfig: This plugin has nothing to configure.
plugins.detail.disabledConfig: This plugin is disabled; enable it to configure.
plugins.detail.noSectionConfig: This section has nothing to configure.
plugins.config.copyFailed: Copy failed; select the text manually
plugins.err.openDesktopOnly: Opening with a system app is available in the desktop app only (a browser has no such bridge)
